# Search efficiency (auto-generated by scripts/search_efficiency.py)

All figures below come from the recorded logs or from the stated arithmetic.

## Cheap multi-fidelity screening (indisputable arithmetic)

- Each step the LLM proposes **20** architectures.
- Only the top **4** by the cheap proxy (5 epochs on 30% of data) are trained in full.
- ⇒ **16 of 20 (80%)** proposals are pruned cheaply; **5× fewer full trainings** per proposal batch.
- In training-epoch terms the saving vs full-fidelity evaluation of every proposal is **≈ 4.0×–4.4×** (for full-training lengths E = 30–60 epochs).

## The bigger picture

- A complete per-dataset search costs on the order of **minutes of GPU** (e.g. Helena ensemble stage = 776 s) plus an **estimated ~$0.09** of LLM API calls.
- The architectures it composes (FT-Transformer, TabM, ...) were originally **hand-designed by research teams over months**. The value is replacing that manual design with an automatic search of comparable quality — see docs/RELATED_WORK.md.
